text:
maria: Heads-up — hearing from ops that some tenants are getting heavy throttles even though abuse-detector reports low scores. thinking we should clarify the signal boundary between rate limiter and abuse heuristics.
kevin: I'm seeing that too. current rate limiter only sees tokens/credits and doesn't ingest the abuse score except for a hard block if score>0.9. means transient spikes flagged by detector won't smoothly influence admission.
jon: sketch: add a lightweight "heuristic layer" in front of admission that normalizes detector scores into soft penalties (probabilistic admission) and exposes a simple API: /heuristic-eval -> {score, penalty_ms, degrade_level}. keeps rate-limiter unaware of internals.
sara: I like decoupling, but careful: extra hop adds latency on the critical path. can we make it async/cache-first? eg evaluate on first request fingerprint, cache for Xs, then let rate limiter consult cache.
maria: exactly. proposed flow: request -> prefilter (heuristic) (cached) -> admission (rate limiter + quotas) -> serve. prefilter only returns a small tuple: low/medium/high + a short TTL. no heavy ML calls on path.
kevin: operationally we need deterministic failure modes. if heuristic returns error, fallback to neutral (no penalty). also need metrics: heuristic_hit, heuristic_miss, applied_penalty.
jon: sample API stub I was thinking:
```
POST /heuristic-eval
body: { tenant_id, fingerprint, route, recent_rate }
resp: { level: "low"|"med"|"high", soft_reject_prob: 0.0-1.0, ttl_seconds: 10 }
```
kevin: that works. rate-limiter can apply probabilistic drop based on soft_reject_prob and otherwise proceed to credit checks. keeps the rate-limiter code simple.
sara: tradeoffs: 1) complexity: new caching layer + extra telemetry 2) risk of signal drift — we need daily calibration with ground-truth 3) fairness: ensure heuristic doesn't bias against small tenants (we should normalize by baseline usage).
maria: rollout plan: feature-flagged canary in staging -> shadow on a few non-critical prod clusters -> 5% traffic experimental with "no-op" sampling AND metric diffing -> gradual enable with AB test comparing latency/cost/false_reject.
jon: ops-bot: scheduled job created to capture calibration dataset every 6h for the first week. job id: abuf-cal-20260318.
ops-bot: created job abuf-cal-20260318, runs on infra-sched. will post results to #incidents after first run.
kevin: one more interface decision: should the heuristic return a numeric score (0..1) or categorical buckets? numeric is flexible but increases coupling. buckets keep contract stable. leaning buckets.
sara: buckets + a hidden numeric in telemetry only (not used by rate limiter) — good compromise.
maria: agreed. action items: kevin to prototype cache layer + fallback behavior, jon to wire API + feature flag, sara to write calibration checklist and fairness normalization tests. I'll schedule a 30m follow-up Thurs.
kevin: starting a PR branch: infra/heuristic-prefilter-proto. will ping when PR ready for review. :thumbsup:
jon: cool, will stub the client in gateway.
sara: adding tests to quota-sim to simulate misclassification and measure fairness impact.
maria: thanks all — this should reduce sudden hard-throttles while keeping abuse defense intact. we can iterate on penalty shaping after we see calibration runs.
